description: Clamshell guide: open the top knee, feet together, to train the side glutes that steady your pelvis. Covers mistakes plus easier and harder versions.
intro: The clamshell is a side-lying move where you open your top knee like a shell while your feet stay together. It targets the side glutes, which keep your pelvis level when you walk, run or stand on one leg. It does not train the pelvic floor directly, but stronger hips give the pelvis better support.
feel: You should feel a warm effort on the outside of the top hip, behind the hip bone. You should not feel it mainly in the front of the thigh or the lower back, and you should keep breathing. Put a hand on your top glute: it should firm as the knee opens. If your back takes over, your hips have probably rolled backward.

mistakes.wrong: Lifting the knee as high as possible
mistakes.right: Open only as far as your hips stay stacked. A small lift with the glute working beats a big one with the pelvis rolling.
Lift for one or two seconds, pause, and lower slowly.
Keep the heels touching so the hip, not the lower leg, drives the movement.

easier: Make the opening smaller, do fewer reps, or rest your head on a pillow so your neck stays relaxed.
harder: Add a light resistance band above the knees, hold the top for three seconds, or lift both feet slightly while you open the knee.
who: Useful for runners, people with weak hips, women after childbirth once cleared, and anyone over 40 who wants better balance and pelvic support.
skip: Check with a doctor or physiotherapist first if lying on your side hurts the hip, after recent hip or pelvic surgery, or with pelvic pain in pregnancy. A pillow between the knees can help. Stop if it hurts.

faq.q: Do clamshells help the pelvic floor?
faq.a: Not directly. They strengthen the side glutes that keep the pelvis stable, which can support pelvic floor work done separately.

faq.q: Why do I feel clamshells in my lower back?
faq.a: Usually your top hip has rolled back. Stack your hips, make the lift smaller and keep your belly gently engaged.
